did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter describes the broad extent of Solomon’s rule: many kingdoms brought him tribute and served him throughout his lifetime.
Did you know? Solomon’s royal court required a very large amount of food each day: thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal.
Did you know? In addition to grain, the daily food supply included ten fattened cattle, twenty cattle from the pasture, and one hundred sheep, as well as other animals and birds.
Did you know? The phrase “each man under his own vine and fig tree” describes the security and peace that prevailed in Judah and Israel during Solomon’s reign, from Dan to Beersheba.
Did you know? The royal administration provided not only food for the king and his guests, but also barley and straw for the horses and other animals, according to each one’s needs.

Did you know? According to the chapter, God granted Solomon wisdom, understanding, and a breadth of heart “as measureless as the sand on the seashore”—an expression of the abundance and depth of his knowledge.
Did you know? Solomon’s wisdom was also expressed through his creative work: he composed three thousand proverbs and wrote one thousand and five songs.
Did you know? Solomon’s wisdom became known internationally: people and kings from many lands came to hear him.
Did you know? Solomon asked Hiram, king of Tyre, for cedar wood from Lebanon because the Israelites were not as skilled at cutting timber as the Sidonians.

Did you know? The cooperation between Solomon and Hiram was based on an exchange of resources: Hiram supplied cedar and cypress timber, while Solomon supplied his household with wheat and oil each year; afterward, the two kings made a treaty.
